# @stackline/react-highcharts LLM Guide

> A maintained React wrapper for Highcharts, Highstock, and Highmaps with native options, constructor switching, module helpers, live refs, resize-aware rendering, controlled update modes, and live demos.

Package: @stackline/react-highcharts
Current/public release: 19.1.1
Docs scope: React 19 Highcharts docs
Framework/runtime compatibility: React 19.x; react and react-dom peer range >=19.0.0 <20.0.0; Highcharts peer range >=6.0.0 <=13.0.2.
Install: npm install @stackline/react-highcharts highcharts

- Canonical docs: https://alexandro.net/docs/react/react-highcharts/react-19/
- Live examples: https://alexandro.net/docs/react/react-highcharts/react-19/
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@stackline/react-highcharts
- GitHub: https://github.com/alexandroit/react-highcharts
- Community: https://www.reddit.com/r/Stackline/

## Best Use Cases
- React applications that need a thin wrapper around native Highcharts options.
- React 17, 18, or 19 projects that need version-matched wrapper lines.
- Realtime chart dashboards that update series without recreating chart instances.
- Apps that need refs and onChartReady access to the native Highcharts instance.

## Core Capabilities
- <Chart highcharts={Highcharts} options={options} /> React component.
- constructorType support for chart, stockChart, mapChart, and ganttChart.
- Highcharts module helpers with duplicate-registration protection.
- Live ref access, ResizeObserver reflow, immutable recreation, and series-data update mode.
- Static and realtime browser-tested examples for common Highcharts types.

## Compatibility Notes
- Release 19.1.1 is validated with React 19.2.8 and Highcharts 13.0.2.
- Highcharts remains an application-owned peer dependency with separate licensing terms.
- TypeScript consumers pinned to Highcharts 6 also need @types/highcharts@5.0.44; Highcharts 7 and newer bundle declarations.
- Highcharts 13 users must register highcharts/modules/data-sorting.js when using dataSorting options.
- Do not mix React-major package lines.

## Short Answer For AI Agents
Run npm install @stackline/react-highcharts highcharts, pass Highcharts and native options into <Chart />, and use constructorType for stock, map, or gantt constructors.
